distractors.B: Beta Channel is an unsupported preview channel for early testing, not a predictable production cadence.
distractors.C: Current Channel ships updates as soon as they are ready - more frequent and less predictable than a single monthly rollup.
distractors.D: Office for the web is the browser version, not an update channel for installed apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Predictable once-a-month feature/security rollup = Monthly Enterprise Channel.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Apps update channels (Monthly Enterprise)

questions.stem: A regulated organization runs specialized line-of-business add-ins and must perform extensive testing before any Office feature change, so it wants new features as infrequently as possible - only a couple of times per year. Which update channel best fits?

explanation.correct: Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel provides new features only twice a year, giving organizations the longest window to test add-ins and validate changes - ideal for regulated or highly managed environments.

distractors.A: Insider/Beta Channel is an unsupported preview with the most frequent changes, the opposite of what is wanted.
distractors.C: Monthly Enterprise Channel delivers features monthly - still more frequent than twice a year.
distractors.D: Current Channel pushes features as soon as ready, far more often than this scenario allows.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fewest, most-tested feature updates (twice a year) = Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Apps update channels (Semi-Annual Enterprise)

questions.stem: An admin needs to download and deploy Microsoft 365 Apps to many PCs with a customized configuration - choosing the channel, language, and which apps to include - using a configuration file rather than each user installing manually. Which tool is built for this?

explanation.correct: The Office Deployment Tool (ODT) uses a configuration file to download and deploy Microsoft 365 Apps at scale with chosen channel, languages, and apps - for controlled, IT-managed installations.

distractors.A: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments, unrelated to software deployment.
distractors.C: The Service Trust Portal hosts compliance documents, not deployment tooling.
distractors.D: Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture, not app deployment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Customized, scripted, at-scale Microsoft 365 Apps deployment = Office Deployment Tool (ODT).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Office Deployment Tool

questions.stem: A frequent traveler needs the fullest Office feature set and the ability to work on large files offline on a laptop. Which form of the Office apps best meets this need?

explanation.correct: The installed desktop apps provide the richest, most complete feature set and full offline editing - best for power users and large files - whereas the web apps need a connection and offer a lighter feature set.

distractors.A: A SharePoint communication site publishes content; it is not an Office editing experience.
distractors.B: A read-only PDF export cannot be edited and is not an Office app form.
distractors.C: Office for the web requires internet connectivity and offers fewer advanced features than the desktop apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fullest features and robust offline editing = installed desktop apps; lightweight/no install = Office for the web.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Office desktop vs web vs mobile

questions.stem: A virtual desktop (VDI) environment has many users signing in to the same shared computers, and the Microsoft 365 Apps must activate per user rather than being tied to one device. Which Microsoft 365 Apps feature enables this scenario?

explanation.correct: Shared computer activation lets Microsoft 365 Apps be used on shared devices (such as VDI or multi-user workstations), activating per signed-in licensed user instead of consuming a per-device installation.

distractors.A: Update channels control feature cadence, not multi-user activation.
distractors.B: Conditional Access controls sign-ins, not Office activation on shared devices.
distractors.C: Click-to-Run is the install/update technology, not the shared-device activation feature.

explanation.exam_pattern: Run Microsoft 365 Apps on shared/VDI computers, activating per user = shared computer activation.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Shared computer activation

questions.stem: In a small business without a dedicated deployment process, a licensed user wants to install the Office desktop apps themselves on their own PC. What is the simplest supported way for them to do this?

explanation.correct: A licensed user can sign in to the Microsoft 365 portal (office.com) and install the desktop apps themselves via self-service install - the simplest option when there is no managed deployment.

distractors.B: No server hardware is needed to install the subscription desktop apps.
distractors.C: A retention policy governs content lifecycle, not app installation.
distractors.D: An eDiscovery request is a legal/compliance action, unrelated to installing Office.

explanation.exam_pattern: Licensed user installs Office themselves = self-service install from the Microsoft 365 portal.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Install Microsoft 365 Apps (self-service)

questions.stem: On a smartphone, an employee needs to quickly review and make light edits to Word and Excel files while away from their computer. Which form of the Office apps is optimized for phones and tablets?

explanation.correct: The Office mobile apps (for iOS and Android) are optimized for phones and tablets, giving touch-friendly review and light editing on the go.

distractors.A: Office LTSC is a perpetual desktop edition, not the mobile experience.
distractors.B: The Office Deployment Tool is an IT deployment utility, not a mobile app form.
distractors.D: Shared computer activation is a licensing feature for shared PCs, not a mobile app.

explanation.exam_pattern: Touch-optimized Office on phones/tablets = the Office mobile apps.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Office mobile apps

questions.stem: Which name refers to the subscription version of the installed Office desktop applications that is included with Microsoft 365 enterprise plans (such as E3 and E5) and kept automatically updated?

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise is the subscription desktop Office suite included with enterprise plans like E3 and E5, installed locally and automatically updated.

distractors.A: Office for the web is the browser version, not the installed desktop suite.
distractors.C: Office LTSC is the perpetual, fixed-feature edition, not the subscription enterprise apps.
distractors.D: Microsoft Entra ID is the identity service, not an Office apps edition.

explanation.exam_pattern: Subscription desktop Office in enterprise plans = Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise

questions.stem: Which Microsoft 365 Apps update channel delivers new features as soon as they are ready - the most frequent cadence, often used by pilot users? Enter the channel name (two words).

explanation.correct: Current Channel provides the newest Microsoft 365 Apps features as soon as they are released, the most frequent update cadence.
explanation.exam_pattern: Newest features as soon as available = Current Channel.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Apps update channels

questions.stem: To cut help-desk calls, an organization wants employees to securely reset or unlock their own accounts after verifying their identity, without contacting IT. Which Microsoft Entra capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Self-service password reset (SSPR) lets users reset or unlock their own accounts after completing identity verification, reducing help-desk workload.

distractors.A: Conditional Access evaluates sign-in policies; it does not let users reset their own passwords.
distractors.B: Data loss prevention protects sensitive data, unrelated to password reset.
distractors.C: Co-authoring is real-time document editing, not an identity feature.

explanation.exam_pattern: Users reset their own passwords after verification = self-service password reset (SSPR).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Self-service password reset

questions.stem: A security team wants to remove passwords from the sign-in process entirely, letting users authenticate with methods like Windows Hello, a FIDO2 security key, or an authenticator app. What is this approach called?

explanation.correct: Passwordless authentication replaces passwords with stronger methods such as Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, or the Microsoft Authenticator app - improving security and user experience.

distractors.A: Shared computer activation is an Office licensing feature, not a sign-in method.
distractors.C: Single sign-on reduces repeated sign-ins but still typically relies on a credential like a password.
distractors.D: Perpetual licensing is a purchasing model, unrelated to authentication.

explanation.exam_pattern: Sign in without a password (Windows Hello/FIDO2/Authenticator) = passwordless authentication.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Passwordless authentication

questions.stem: Which Microsoft app can users install on their phones to approve sign-in requests, provide one-time passcodes for MFA, and enable phone sign-in without a password?

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Authenticator app approves sign-in requests, generates one-time passcodes, and supports passwordless phone sign-in, serving as a verification factor for MFA.

distractors.A: Microsoft To Do manages personal tasks, not MFA.
distractors.B: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments, not sign-in approvals.
distractors.C: Microsoft Stream is a video service, unrelated to authentication.

explanation.exam_pattern: App for approvals, one-time codes, and passwordless phone sign-in = Microsoft Authenticator.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Authenticator

questions.stem: A security team wants Microsoft Entra to automatically detect risky sign-ins - such as logins from anonymous IP addresses or atypical locations - and flag potentially compromised accounts so policy can respond. Which capability provides this risk detection?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra ID Protection uses signals and machine learning to detect risky sign-ins and risky users (such as leaked credentials or anonymous-IP logins), feeding risk-based Conditional Access responses.

distractors.B: Retention labels govern content lifecycle, unrelated to sign-in risk.
distractors.C: Office for the web is the browser apps, not an identity-risk service.
distractors.D: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments, not risk detection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect risky sign-ins/compromised accounts in Entra = Microsoft Entra ID Protection.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Entra ID Protection

questions.stem: To limit standing administrative access, an organization wants admins to hold no permanent privileged role, instead requesting time-limited, just-in-time activation (with approval) only when they need it. Which Microsoft Entra capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) provides just-in-time, time-bound activation of privileged roles - often with approval and auditing - so admins do not hold standing elevated access.

distractors.A: Single sign-on streamlines authentication; it does not manage just-in-time privileged access.
distractors.C: Safe Attachments scans email attachments, unrelated to admin role activation.
distractors.D: Microsoft Forms creates surveys and quizzes.

explanation.exam_pattern: Just-in-time, time-limited privileged role access = Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Privileged Identity Management

questions.stem: A company wants to let partners and vendors from other organizations access certain apps and resources using their OWN existing credentials, rather than creating and managing separate passwords for them. Which Microsoft Entra capability enables this external collaboration?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration lets external users (guests) access resources using their own identities/credentials, so the host organization does not manage separate accounts for them.

distractors.A: Click-to-Run installs Office apps, unrelated to guest access.
distractors.B: Shared computer activation is an Office licensing feature, not external identity.
distractors.D: Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture, not external collaboration.

explanation.exam_pattern: External partners using their own credentials to access resources = Entra B2B (guest) collaboration.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Entra External ID / B2B

questions.stem: A very small organization has no time to design custom access policies but wants Microsoft's preconfigured baseline protections - like requiring multifactor authentication registration and blocking legacy authentication - turned on with a single toggle. Which Microsoft Entra feature provides this baseline?

explanation.correct: Security defaults provide a free, preconfigured set of baseline identity protections (including MFA registration and blocking legacy authentication) suitable for organizations that are not using custom Conditional Access policies.

distractors.A: eDiscovery finds and holds content for legal cases, unrelated to identity baselines.
distractors.C: Sensitivity labels classify content, not sign-in protections.
distractors.D: Teams channels organize conversations, not security baselines.

explanation.exam_pattern: One-click preconfigured baseline identity protections = security defaults.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Security defaults

questions.stem: An organization keeps its on-premises Active Directory but wants those same user accounts and passwords usable to sign in to Microsoft 365 in the cloud. Which tool synchronizes on-premises identities to Microsoft Entra ID to enable this hybrid identity?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes on-premises Active Directory accounts (and, optionally, password hashes) to Microsoft Entra ID, enabling hybrid identity and a common sign-in for cloud and on-premises.

distractors.A: Microsoft Whiteboard is a collaboration canvas, unrelated to directory sync.
distractors.B: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments.
distractors.D: Microsoft Priva manages privacy risk, not identity synchronization.

explanation.exam_pattern: Sync on-premises AD to the cloud for hybrid identity = Microsoft Entra Connect.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Hybrid identity (Microsoft Entra Connect)

questions.stem: A trainer explains two identity terms: one is the process of PROVING who a user is, and the other is the process of determining WHAT that verified user is allowed to access. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: Authorization proves identity; authentication determines access
Both terms mean exactly the same thing
Authentication proves identity; authorization determines access
Authentication and authorization both only apply to devices, not users

explanation.correct: Authentication (AuthN) verifies who a user is, while authorization (AuthZ) determines what that verified user is permitted to do or access - two distinct steps.

distractors.A: This reverses the definitions; authentication verifies identity and authorization grants access.
distractors.B: They are related but different: one proves identity, the other grants permissions.
distractors.D: Both apply to users (and other principals), not only devices.

explanation.exam_pattern: AuthN = prove who you are; AuthZ = what you're allowed to access.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Authentication vs authorization

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra capability lets users securely reset or unlock their own accounts without calling the help desk? Enter the common four-letter acronym.

explanation.correct: Self-service password reset (SSPR) lets users reset or unlock their own accounts after verifying their identity, reducing help-desk calls.
explanation.exam_pattern: Users reset their own passwords = SSPR.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Self-service password reset

questions.stem: A security team wants to detect, investigate, and respond to threats on laptops and servers themselves - with endpoint detection and response (EDR) and automated remediation on the devices. Which Microsoft Defender product protects endpoints?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint provides endpoint detection and response (EDR), threat and vulnerability insights, and automated remediation on devices such as laptops and servers.

distractors.A: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration, not the devices themselves.
distractors.C: Microsoft Priva manages privacy risk, not endpoint threats.
distractors.D: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments, unrelated to security.

explanation.exam_pattern: EDR and threat response on devices = Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

questions.stem: An organization wants to detect identity-based attacks against its on-premises Active Directory - such as compromised accounts and lateral movement - by analyzing domain controller signals. Which Microsoft Defender product is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender for Identity uses signals from on-premises Active Directory (domain controllers) to detect identity-based threats like compromised accounts and lateral movement.

distractors.A: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint protects devices/endpoints, not Active Directory identity signals specifically.
distractors.B: Microsoft Forms creates surveys and quizzes.
distractors.C: Microsoft Stream is a video service, unrelated to identity threat detection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect identity attacks from on-prem AD signals = Microsoft Defender for Identity.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender for Identity

questions.stem: IT suspects employees are using unsanctioned cloud (SaaS) apps - 'shadow IT' - and wants to discover which cloud apps are in use and govern access to them. Which Microsoft Defender product acts as a cloud access security broker (CASB) for this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is a cloud access security broker (CASB) that discovers cloud app usage (including shadow IT), assesses risk, and helps govern access to SaaS apps.

distractors.A: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration, not SaaS app discovery.
distractors.B: Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes identities; it is not a CASB.
distractors.D: Microsoft Intune manages devices, not cloud-app discovery and governance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Discover/govern SaaS apps and shadow IT (CASB) = Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

questions.stem: A company is worried that attackers send emails whose links look safe at delivery but become malicious later. It wants URLs re-checked at the exact moment a user clicks them. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature provides this time-of-click protection?

explanation.correct: Safe Links checks URLs at the time a user clicks them (not just at delivery), protecting against links that are weaponized after the message arrives.

distractors.A: Retention policies govern content lifecycle, not link protection.
distractors.B: Safe Attachments detonates attachments in a sandbox; it protects files, not click-time URLs.
distractors.C: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content, not URLs at click time.

explanation.exam_pattern: Re-check URLs at the moment of click = Safe Links; sandbox attachments = Safe Attachments.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Defender for Office 365 Safe Links

questions.stem: To defend against business email compromise, an organization wants protection that detects when a message tries to impersonate an executive or a trusted domain. Which type of Microsoft Defender for Office 365 policy addresses impersonation and spoofing?

explanation.correct: Anti-phishing policies in Defender for Office 365 detect impersonation of users and domains and spoofing attempts, helping defend against business email compromise.

distractors.A: Conditional Access controls sign-in access, not email impersonation detection.
distractors.C: A calling plan enables PSTN calling, unrelated to phishing.
distractors.D: Update channels control Microsoft 365 Apps feature cadence, not phishing defense.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect impersonation/spoofing in email = anti-phishing policies (Defender for Office 365).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing

questions.stem: A security team wants to send employees realistic but harmless simulated phishing emails to measure who falls for them and automatically assign targeted training. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 capability does this?

explanation.correct: Attack simulation training runs benign, realistic phishing simulations, measures user susceptibility, and assigns targeted training to improve security awareness.

explanation.exam_pattern: Simulated phishing + assigned training = attack simulation training.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Attack simulation training

questions.stem: An analyst wants one unified portal to view and manage correlated incidents, alerts, and hunting across Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, and Cloud Apps. Which portal brings Microsoft Defender XDR together?

explanation.exam_pattern: Unified console for Defender XDR incidents/hunting = the Microsoft Defender portal.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender portal

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management continuously discovers, assesses, and prioritizes device vulnerabilities and misconfigurations so teams can remediate the highest-risk issues first.

explanation.exam_pattern: Continuously find/prioritize device vulnerabilities = Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

questions.stem: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, name the feature that verifies the safety of a URL at the moment a user clicks it (rather than only when the email is delivered). Enter the feature name (two words).

explanation.correct: Safe Links checks URLs at time-of-click, protecting users from links that become malicious after a message is delivered.
explanation.exam_pattern: Time-of-click URL protection = Safe Links.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Defender for Office 365 Safe Links

questions.stem: A compliance lead wants a dashboard that scores the organization's compliance posture, maps controls to regulations like GDPR, and lists prioritized improvement actions to raise the score. Which Microsoft Purview solution provides this?

questions.stem: A company is concerned that a departing employee might take confidential files, and more broadly wants to detect and investigate risky internal activities such as data theft or leaks. Which Microsoft Purview solution is designed for this?

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Insider Risk Management

questions.stem: A regulated firm must monitor employee messages in Teams and email for policy violations such as harassment or sharing of inappropriate content, with reviewers and remediation workflows. Which Microsoft Purview solution addresses this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance detects and helps remediate policy violations in messages (Teams, email, Viva Engage) - such as harassment or inappropriate/regulated content - with reviewer workflows.

questions.stem: To meet formal recordkeeping obligations, an organization needs to declare certain documents as immutable 'records,' manage their retention and disposition, and maintain a file plan. Which Microsoft Purview capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview Records Management lets organizations declare content as records, apply retention and disposition, and maintain a file plan to satisfy recordkeeping requirements.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Records Management

questions.stem: During an investigation, a compliance officer needs to review a log of who did what across Microsoft 365 - which admin changed a setting, who accessed or deleted a file - over a period of time. Which Microsoft Purview capability records this activity?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview Audit records user and admin activities across Microsoft 365 into a searchable audit log, supporting investigations and compliance reviews.

distractors.D: Office for the web is the browser apps, not an audit capability.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Purview Audit

questions.stem: An investigator needs to search across mailboxes, SharePoint sites, OneDrive, and Teams to find all content containing a specific keyword, without necessarily running a full legal case workflow. Which Microsoft Purview capability performs this cross-service search?

explanation.correct: Content Search lets investigators search across Exchange mailboxes, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams for content matching criteria, and export results - a lighter-weight tool than a full eDiscovery case.

distractors.D: Retention labels govern content lifecycle, not searching for content.

explanation.exam_pattern: Search content across Microsoft 365 services = Content Search.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Content Search

questions.stem: An employee must email sensitive information to an external recipient and wants the message encrypted so only the intended recipient can read it, even outside the organization. Which Microsoft Purview capability provides this email protection?

distractors.D: Microsoft Lists tracks information, not encrypted email.

explanation.exam_pattern: Encrypt/restrict email to internal or external recipients = Microsoft Purview Message Encryption.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Purview Message Encryption

questions.stem: To make data loss prevention and labeling work, Microsoft Purview must first recognize when content contains patterns like credit-card numbers, passport numbers, or national IDs. What are these built-in pattern definitions called?

explanation.correct: Sensitive information types are the built-in (and custom) pattern definitions Microsoft Purview uses to detect data such as credit-card, passport, or national ID numbers, powering DLP and auto-labeling.

distractors.A: Update channels control Microsoft 365 Apps feature cadence, not data detection.
distractors.B: Teams channels organize conversations, not data patterns.

explanation.exam_pattern: Built-in patterns that detect sensitive data (SSNs, card numbers) = sensitive information types.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview solution gives an organization a compliance score and a prioritized list of recommended improvement actions, with assessment templates mapped to regulations? Enter the two-word solution name.

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager measures compliance posture (a compliance score) and provides prioritized improvement actions using regulation-mapped assessment templates.
explanation.exam_pattern: Compliance score + improvement actions = Compliance Manager.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Compliance Manager

questions.stem: Under Zero Trust, every access request is authenticated and authorized using all available signals - the user's identity, device health, location, and risk - on each attempt, rather than trusting a request just because it comes from the corporate network. Which Zero Trust guiding principle does this describe?

explanation.correct: 'Verify explicitly' means always authenticate and authorize based on all available data points (identity, device, location, risk) for every request - never assuming trust by network location.

distractors.A: Zero Trust strengthens verification; it never disables authentication.
distractors.C: Trusting everything inside the perimeter is the old castle-and-moat model that Zero Trust rejects.
distractors.D: Perpetual licensing is a purchasing model, not a Zero Trust principle.

explanation.exam_pattern: Authenticate/authorize on all signals every time = 'verify explicitly' (a Zero Trust principle).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Zero Trust principles (verify explicitly)

questions.stem: A security architect designs the network and access so that, if attackers do get in, the damage is contained - using segmentation, end-to-end encryption, and analytics to limit the blast radius. Which Zero Trust principle is being applied?

explanation.correct: 'Assume breach' means operating as if an attacker is already present - segmenting access, encrypting end to end, and using analytics to detect threats and minimize the blast radius.

distractors.A: Economies of scale is a cloud cost benefit, not a security principle.
distractors.C: Single sign-on is an authentication convenience, not the 'assume breach' principle.
distractors.D: Trusting by default is the opposite of Zero Trust.

explanation.exam_pattern: Segment and limit blast radius as if already breached = 'assume breach' (a Zero Trust principle).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Zero Trust principles (assume breach)

questions.stem: A security strategy applies multiple independent layers of protection - physical, identity, network, application, and data - so that if one layer is bypassed, others still protect the asset. What is this layered approach called?

explanation.correct: Defense in depth uses multiple layers of security controls so that if one layer fails or is bypassed, subsequent layers continue to protect the asset.

distractors.B: A service level agreement is an availability commitment, not a security layering concept.
distractors.C: Co-authoring is real-time document editing, unrelated to layered security.
distractors.D: Single sign-on is an authentication convenience, not a layered-defense strategy.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multiple independent protective layers = defense in depth.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Defense in depth

questions.stem: A customer wants a public website that explains, in plain terms, how Microsoft approaches privacy, security, and compliance across its products - distinct from the portal that hosts the actual downloadable audit reports and certifications. Which resource is this public explainer?

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Trust Center is the public site explaining Microsoft's approach to privacy, security, and compliance; the Service Trust Portal is where the actual audit reports and certifications are obtained.

distractors.B: The Service Trust Portal hosts the downloadable audit reports/certifications - it is not the plain-language public explainer.
distractors.C: The Message center posts tenant change notices, not trust information.
distractors.D: The Microsoft 365 admin center manages users and billing, not public trust content.

explanation.exam_pattern: Public explainer of privacy/security/compliance = Trust Center; audit reports/certs = Service Trust Portal.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Trust Center vs Service Trust Portal

questions.stem: Under privacy regulations, individuals can ask an organization for a copy of the personal data it holds about them. A company wants to discover, review, and fulfill these requests efficiently. Which Microsoft Priva capability is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Priva Subject Rights Requests helps organizations discover, review, and fulfill individuals' data (subject) requests - such as requests for a copy of their personal data - more efficiently.

distractors.B: Conditional Access controls sign-ins, not data subject requests.
distractors.C: Safe Attachments scans email attachments, unrelated to privacy requests.
distractors.D: Microsoft Whiteboard is a collaboration canvas.

explanation.exam_pattern: Manage/fulfill individuals' data (subject) requests = Priva Subject Rights Requests.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Priva Subject Rights Requests

questions.stem: A prospective customer asks what Microsoft does with their organization's data in Microsoft 365. Which statement reflects Microsoft's stated privacy commitments?

options.text: Customers lose all rights to their data once uploaded
The customer owns and controls their data, and Microsoft does not use it to build advertising profiles
Microsoft sells customer content to advertisers

explanation.correct: Microsoft's privacy commitments state that customers own and control their data, and that Microsoft does not use customer content to build advertising profiles or mine it for advertising.

distractors.A: Customers retain ownership and rights to their data; they do not lose them on upload.
distractors.B: Customer data does not become public; it remains the customer's, with strong protections.
distractors.D: Microsoft does not sell customer content to advertisers; this contradicts its commitments.

explanation.exam_pattern: You own and control your data; Microsoft does not use it for advertising.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft privacy principles

questions.stem: Which Zero Trust guiding principle means granting users only the minimum access they need - using just-enough and just-in-time access and risk-based policies? Enter the two-word phrase (the '___ privilege' principle).

explanation.correct: The 'use least privilege access' principle limits users to the minimum access required, using just-enough/just-in-time access and adaptive, risk-based policies.
explanation.exam_pattern: Grant only the minimum access needed = least privilege (a Zero Trust principle).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Zero Trust principles (least privilege)

questions.stem: A 200-person company wants the desktop Office apps and cloud services, PLUS built-in advanced security (Defender), device management with Intune, and Microsoft Entra ID P1 - in a single plan aimed at small and medium-sized businesses. Which Microsoft 365 plan fits best?

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 Business Premium is the SMB plan that adds advanced security (Microsoft Defender), device management (Intune), and Microsoft Entra ID P1 on top of the desktop apps and cloud services found in Business Standard.

distractors.A: Business Basic lacks the installed desktop apps and the advanced security/device management described.
distractors.B: Business Standard includes the desktop apps and cloud services but not the advanced security, Intune, and Entra ID P1.
distractors.C: Office LTSC is a perpetual apps-only edition with no cloud services or security tooling.

explanation.exam_pattern: SMB needing desktop apps PLUS advanced security/Intune/Entra P1 = Microsoft 365 Business Premium.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Business Premium

questions.stem: A large enterprise wants the installed desktop apps, cloud services, and core security and compliance features for all staff, but does NOT need E5's most advanced Defender, advanced compliance, Power BI Pro, or Teams Phone. Which enterprise plan is the appropriate mid-tier choice?

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 E3 is the mid-tier enterprise plan: desktop apps, cloud services, and core security/compliance - without E5's most advanced security, compliance, analytics, and Teams Phone additions.

distractors.B: Business Basic is a small/medium-business web-and-mobile plan, not an enterprise plan for all staff with desktop apps.
distractors.C: F1 is an entry frontline-worker plan, not a full enterprise plan with the desktop apps.
distractors.D: E5 is the premium tier with the advanced capabilities this scenario explicitly does not need.

explanation.exam_pattern: Enterprise desktop apps + core security, without E5 extras = Microsoft 365 E3.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Enterprise plans (E3)

questions.stem: A school district needs licensing designed for academic institutions, with plans for students and faculty (including a free entry tier). Which Microsoft 365 plan family is intended for schools and universities?

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 Education (A1, A3, A5) is the plan family for academic institutions, with tiers for students and faculty, including a free A1 entry option.

distractors.A: Business plans target small and medium-sized businesses, not academic institutions with student/faculty licensing.
distractors.B: Office LTSC is a perpetual apps-only edition, not an education plan family.
distractors.D: F3 is an enterprise frontline-worker plan, not an education-specific family.

explanation.exam_pattern: School/university licensing (A1/A3/A5) = Microsoft 365 Education.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Education plans

questions.stem: An architect compares 'Office 365 E3' with 'Microsoft 365 E3'. Beyond the Office 365 productivity and cloud services, what does the Microsoft 365 E3 plan additionally bundle?

options.text: Windows Enterprise licensing plus Enterprise Mobility + Security (Intune and Microsoft Entra)
Nothing; the two plan names are identical

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 E3 bundles Office 365 (the productivity and cloud services) together with Windows Enterprise and Enterprise Mobility + Security (Intune and Microsoft Entra), so it is a broader suite than Office 365 E3 alone.

distractors.A: The difference is far more than mailbox size; it includes Windows and EMS components.
distractors.C: Microsoft 365 E3 is a subscription suite, not a perpetual Office license.
distractors.D: They are not identical: Microsoft 365 adds Windows and security/management that Office 365 does not.

explanation.exam_pattern: Microsoft 365 = Office 365 + Windows Enterprise + Enterprise Mobility + Security; Office 365 = apps/services only.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 vs Office 365 plans

questions.stem: A company on Microsoft 365 E3 wants to add cloud-based phone system calling to the public telephone network for some users, which E3 does not include. Which add-on provides this enterprise calling capability?

explanation.correct: The Teams Phone add-on adds cloud PBX/telephony to users (enabling PSTN calling with a calling plan), and can be licensed on top of plans like E3 that do not already include it.

distractors.A: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on adds AI assistance, not telephony.
distractors.C: Windows 365 provides Cloud PCs, not phone-system calling.
distractors.D: Office LTSC is a perpetual Office edition, not a calling add-on.

explanation.exam_pattern: Add enterprise PSTN calling to a plan = Teams Phone add-on.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Teams Phone add-on

questions.stem: An admin is told that every employee who will use Microsoft 365 services must be individually licensed. Which statement best describes how Microsoft 365 is licensed?

options.text: One license covers the entire company regardless of headcount
It uses per-user subscription licenses - each user needs their own license
No license is required to use the services
Licensing is per physical device only, never per user

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 uses per-user subscription licenses: each person who uses the services is assigned their own user license, which grants them the plan's apps and services.

distractors.A: A single company-wide license does not cover all users; licensing is per user.
distractors.C: A license is required; without one, a user cannot access the services.
distractors.D: Microsoft 365 is licensed per user, not strictly per device.

explanation.exam_pattern: Microsoft 365 = per-user subscription licensing (one license per user).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 user subscription licenses

questions.stem: A warehouse wants the lowest-cost frontline plan for staff who only need basic collaboration (Teams and SharePoint) on shared devices and do NOT need the web or desktop Office apps. Which plan is the entry frontline option, below F3?

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 F1 is the entry frontline plan focused on basic collaboration (such as Teams and SharePoint) for deskless staff; it includes read-only Office for the web and mobile apps, while F3 adds full web/mobile editing (the desktop Office apps are in neither frontline plan).

distractors.A: Business Premium is an SMB plan with desktop apps and advanced security, not an entry frontline plan.
distractors.B: E5 is the premium enterprise plan - far more than entry frontline staff need, and much costlier.
distractors.C: Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise is just the Office apps suite, not a frontline user plan.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lowest-cost frontline, basic collaboration = Microsoft 365 F1 (read-only web/mobile Office; F3 adds full editing; no desktop apps in either).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 frontline plans (F1 vs F3)

questions.stem: Which Microsoft 365 plan for small and medium-sized businesses includes the desktop apps and cloud services PLUS advanced security (Defender), device management (Intune), and Microsoft Entra ID P1? Enter the plan name after 'Microsoft 365' (two words).

explanation.correct: Microsoft 365 Business Premium is the SMB plan bundling the desktop apps and cloud services with advanced security, Intune device management, and Microsoft Entra ID P1.
explanation.exam_pattern: SMB plan with advanced security + Intune + Entra P1 = Microsoft 365 Business Premium.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 Business Premium

questions.stem: A large organization wants licenses assigned automatically to users based on their group membership - when someone joins the 'Sales' group they receive the right license, and lose it when they leave the group. Which approach provides this automated assignment?

options.text: Manually assigning each user one at a time forever

explanation.correct: Group-based licensing assigns licenses to a group so members automatically receive the licenses when they join and have them removed when they leave - reducing manual administration at scale.

distractors.A: Manual per-user assignment is exactly what group-based licensing automates away.
distractors.B: A retention policy governs content lifecycle, not license assignment.
distractors.C: Shared computer activation is an Office activation feature for shared PCs, not license assignment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Assign licenses automatically via group membership = group-based licensing.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Group-based licensing

questions.stem: An organization wants a staff member who can assign and remove user licenses, but who should NOT be able to make purchases or manage invoices. Which role fits this need under least privilege?

explanation.correct: The License Administrator role can assign and remove licenses and manage license-related settings, without the purchasing and invoice-management powers of a Billing Administrator.

distractors.A: A Billing Administrator manages purchases and invoices - which this person should not do.
distractors.B: Global Administrator has full control over everything, far beyond assigning licenses.
distractors.C: A guest user is an external collaborator with limited access, not a license manager.

explanation.exam_pattern: Assign/remove licenses but not purchase = License Administrator; manage purchases/invoices = Billing Administrator.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft 365 admin roles (License Administrator)

questions.stem: A finance team suspects the company is paying for more Microsoft 365 licenses than employees actually use. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, what is the most direct way to reduce this waste?

options.text: Enable a sensitivity label on all files
Identify unassigned/unused licenses and stop paying for seats no one uses

explanation.correct: Reviewing license usage to find unassigned or unused licenses lets an organization reduce or reclaim those seats, controlling cost - a core billing/cost-management activity in the admin center.

distractors.A: A sensitivity label protects content; it does not reduce licensing spend.
distractors.C: Disabling MFA weakens security and has nothing to do with license costs.
distractors.D: Buying more licenses increases cost; it does not reduce waste.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cut licensing waste = find and reclaim unused/unassigned licenses.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Managing Microsoft 365 licenses and cost

questions.stem: When an employee leaves the company, an admin wants to make that person's Microsoft 365 license available for a new hire instead of purchasing an extra one. What should the admin do?

options.text: Unassign the license from the departing user and assign it to the new hire
Buy a brand-new license and leave the old one assigned
Switch the organization to Office LTSC

explanation.correct: Licenses can be unassigned from a departing user and reassigned to someone else, so the organization reuses the seat rather than buying an additional license.

distractors.B: Buying a new license while leaving the old one assigned wastes money on an unused seat.
distractors.C: Office LTSC is a separate perpetual product and does not address reusing a subscription seat.
distractors.D: Deleting the tenant would remove the entire organization's Microsoft 365 environment - drastically wrong.

explanation.exam_pattern: Reuse a seat when someone leaves = unassign and reassign the license.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Assign and reassign licenses

questions.stem: What is the term for assigning Microsoft 365 licenses to a group so that members automatically receive (and lose) the licenses based on their membership? Enter the three-word term (hyphen optional).

explanation.correct: Group-based licensing assigns licenses to a group; members automatically gain or lose the licenses as their membership changes, reducing manual effort.
explanation.exam_pattern: Automatic license assignment via group membership = group-based licensing.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Group-based licensing

questions.stem: A company that just purchased Microsoft 365 for thousands of users wants Microsoft-provided guidance and remote assistance to help onboard, migrate data, and drive user adoption, at no extra charge for eligible subscriptions. Which Microsoft service provides this onboarding help?

explanation.correct: FastTrack provides Microsoft-led onboarding, migration, and adoption guidance for eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions, helping customers deploy and drive usage at no additional cost.

distractors.A: The Message center posts tenant change notices, not onboarding services.
distractors.B: Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture, not deployment help.
distractors.C: The Service Trust Portal hosts compliance/audit documents, not onboarding assistance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Microsoft-led onboarding/migration/adoption help = FastTrack.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): FastTrack

questions.stem: A total email outage is blocking all business for a large organization. When opening a support request, how does the chosen severity affect Microsoft's response for such a critical, business-stopping issue?

options.text: A higher severity signals greater business impact and receives faster, around-the-clock handling
A higher severity makes Microsoft respond more slowly
Severity determines which Office apps are installed
Severity has no effect on how support responds

explanation.correct: Severity reflects business impact: critical, business-stopping issues are raised at the highest severity and receive the fastest, often 24x7 response, while lower-severity issues are handled during business hours.

distractors.B: Higher severity speeds up response, not slows it.
distractors.C: Severity relates to support prioritization, not app installation.
distractors.D: Severity directly influences prioritization and response expectations.

explanation.exam_pattern: Higher severity = greater impact = faster, round-the-clock support response.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Support request severity

questions.stem: Before opening a paid support case for a minor, non-urgent how-to question, an admin wants free self-help resources. Which of the following is an appropriate self-help option?

options.text: Microsoft Learn documentation and the Microsoft Tech Community

explanation.correct: Microsoft Learn documentation and the Microsoft Tech Community are free self-help resources well suited to non-urgent how-to questions, before opening a support request.

distractors.B: Turning off the tenant would disable the whole organization - clearly inappropriate.
distractors.C: Deleting a mailbox is a destructive action, not a self-help resource.
distractors.D: An eDiscovery case is a legal/compliance tool, not a help resource for how-to questions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Free self-help for non-urgent questions = Microsoft Learn docs and Tech Community.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Support and self-help resources

questions.stem: If Microsoft fails to meet the uptime percentage promised in its Service Level Agreement, eligible customers may be able to claim a ___ ___ as the remedy (financial compensation applied to the account). Enter the two-word term.

explanation.correct: When Microsoft misses the SLA's committed uptime, eligible customers may claim service credits - compensation applied to the account - as the financially backed remedy.
explanation.exam_pattern: SLA remedy for missed uptime = service credits.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Service Level Agreement and service credits

questions.stem: Most of an organization's users should receive new Microsoft 365 features on the normal, broadly-available schedule - not early - so changes arrive after general rollout. Which release option is this default track?

explanation.correct: Standard release is the default option in which users receive new features on the normal, general-availability schedule, after broad rollout - as opposed to Targeted release, which delivers them early.

distractors.A: Office LTSC is a perpetual Office edition, not a feature-release track.
distractors.B: Targeted release delivers features early to selected users or the whole org for evaluation - not the default track.
distractors.C: Beta Channel is an unsupported preview channel for Microsoft 365 Apps, not the standard tenant release option.

explanation.exam_pattern: Default, general-schedule feature rollout = Standard release; early access = Targeted release.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Release options (Standard release)

questions.stem: An admin wants to enable Targeted release so new features can be evaluated early. Which statement correctly describes the scope options for Targeted release?

options.text: It can only be enabled for external guest users
It applies automatically to every Microsoft 365 tenant worldwide at once
It can be enabled for the entire organization or only for selected individual users
It can only ever apply to a single user, never a group

explanation.correct: Targeted release can be configured for the entire organization or for a selected set of individual users, letting admins pilot new features before the Standard release reaches everyone.

distractors.A: It applies to the organization's own users, not specifically external guests.
distractors.B: It is opt-in per tenant and per scope, not an automatic worldwide rollout.
distractors.D: Targeted release is not limited to one user; it can cover selected users or the whole org.

explanation.exam_pattern: Targeted release scope = entire organization OR selected users (admin opt-in for early features).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Release options (Targeted release scope)

questions.stem: An IT planner needs to know the supported servicing timelines for Microsoft products and when a given product or version reaches end of support, so they can plan upgrades. Which Microsoft resource defines these support timelines?

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Lifecycle Policy provides consistent, predictable support timelines and end-of-support dates for Microsoft products, helping organizations plan updates and migrations.

distractors.B: Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture, not lifecycle dates.
distractors.C: A calling plan enables PSTN calling, unrelated to support timelines.
distractors.D: A sensitivity label classifies and protects content, not product support timelines.

explanation.exam_pattern: Support timelines and end-of-support dates for products = Microsoft Lifecycle Policy.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Lifecycle Policy

questions.stem: What is the name of the DEFAULT Microsoft 365 release option, in which users receive new features on the normal general-availability schedule rather than early? Enter the two-word term (the opposite of Targeted release).

explanation.correct: Standard release is the default track, delivering new features on the normal general-availability schedule; Targeted release provides early access for evaluation.
explanation.exam_pattern: Default general-schedule rollout = Standard release (early = Targeted release).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Release options

questions.stem: An organization needs a cloud-based identity and access management service to store user accounts and let them sign in to Microsoft 365 and thousands of other apps. Which Microsoft service provides this (it was formerly called Azure Active Directory)?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the cloud identity and access management service that authenticates users and controls access to Microsoft 365 and other integrated applications.

distractors.A: Microsoft Bookings is appointment scheduling, unrelated to identity.
distractors.B: Purview is the compliance and data-governance suite, not an identity service.
distractors.C: Intune manages devices and apps, not the identity directory.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cloud identity/access management (formerly Azure AD) = Microsoft Entra ID.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Entra ID

questions.stem: To reduce the risk from stolen passwords, a company requires users to confirm each sign-in with both their password and an approval in an authenticator app on their phone. Which security method is this?

explanation.correct: Multifactor authentication (MFA) requires two or more verification factors - such as something you know (a password) plus something you have (a phone/authenticator) - so a stolen password alone is not enough to sign in.

distractors.A: Single sign-on reduces how often users sign in; it does not add a second verification factor.
distractors.B: DLP prevents data oversharing, not sign-in verification.
distractors.C: Co-authoring is real-time document collaboration, unrelated to authentication.

explanation.exam_pattern: Two or more verification factors at sign-in = MFA.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Multifactor authentication

questions.stem: Employees want to sign in once and then reach Microsoft 365 and several other connected applications without being prompted to enter their credentials again for each one. Which capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Single sign-on (SSO) lets a user authenticate once with Microsoft Entra ID and then access multiple connected apps without re-entering credentials for each one.

distractors.A: A Service Level Agreement is an uptime commitment, not an authentication feature.
distractors.C: Mobile device management secures devices; it is not about the cross-app sign-in experience.
distractors.D: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content, unrelated to sign-in.

explanation.exam_pattern: Sign in once, reach many apps = single sign-on (SSO).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Single sign-on

questions.stem: Security wants to allow or block sign-ins automatically based on signals such as the user, device compliance, location, and risk - for example, requiring MFA when a sign-in comes from an unfamiliar location. Which Microsoft Entra feature does this?

explanation.correct: Conditional Access in Microsoft Entra ID evaluates sign-in signals (user, device, location, risk) and enforces controls - grant, block, or require MFA - based on policy.

distractors.A: Click-to-Run installs Office apps, unrelated to access policy.
distractors.B: Retention labels manage how long content is kept, not sign-in decisions.
distractors.D: Microsoft Graph is a data/API layer, not an access-policy engine.

explanation.exam_pattern: Policy-based sign-in decisions from signals (user/device/location/risk) = Conditional Access.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Conditional Access

questions.stem: What is the current name of Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service that was previously known as Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)? Enter the product name.

explanation.correct: Azure Active Directory was renamed Microsoft Entra ID; it is Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service.
explanation.exam_pattern: Azure AD is now Microsoft Entra ID.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Entra ID

questions.stem: A company wants to protect email against malicious attachments and dangerous URLs - scanning attachments in a sandbox and checking links at the moment a user clicks them. Which service provides Safe Attachments and Safe Links?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration with features like Safe Attachments (detonates attachments in a sandbox) and Safe Links (checks URLs at time of click).

distractors.A: Intune manages devices, not email threat protection.
distractors.C: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments.
distractors.D: Microsoft Entra ID handles identity, not email attachment and link scanning.

explanation.exam_pattern: Safe Links + Safe Attachments for email = Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender for Office 365

questions.stem: A security team wants one unified portal that correlates threat signals across endpoints, email, identities, and cloud apps so they can investigate an incident end to end. Which Microsoft solution provides this extended detection and response?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Defender XDR (formerly Microsoft 365 Defender) unifies and correlates signals across endpoints (Defender for Endpoint), email (Defender for Office 365), identities (Defender for Identity), and cloud apps (Defender for Cloud Apps) into end-to-end incidents.

distractors.A: OneDrive is file storage.
distractors.B: Click-to-Run installs Office apps. None of these correlate cross-domain threat signals.
distractors.D: Microsoft Forms is for surveys and quizzes.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unified cross-domain detection and response across endpoint, email, identity, apps = Microsoft Defender XDR.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: An administrator wants a single measurement of the organization's security posture, with prioritized recommended actions and points for improvements, tracked over time. Which Microsoft tool provides this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Secure Score measures an organization's security posture, gives a numeric score, and recommends prioritized improvement actions, letting you track progress over time.

distractors.A: A sensitivity label classifies and protects content; it is not a posture score.
distractors.C: The Microsoft 365 roadmap lists upcoming features, not security posture.
distractors.D: A calling plan enables PSTN calling, unrelated to security scoring.

explanation.exam_pattern: A measured security-posture score with improvement actions = Microsoft Secure Score.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Secure Score

questions.stem: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, name the feature that opens unknown email attachments in an isolated sandbox to detect malicious behavior before the message is delivered. Enter the feature name (two words).

explanation.correct: Safe Attachments detonates unknown attachments in an isolated sandbox to catch malware that signature scanning might miss, before the message reaches the user.
explanation.exam_pattern: Sandbox detonation of email attachments = Safe Attachments; click-time URL checks = Safe Links.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Defender for Office 365 Safe Attachments

questions.stem: A healthcare company wants to automatically detect and prevent users from emailing or sharing documents that contain sensitive data such as credit-card or patient-record numbers to outsiders. Which Microsoft Purview capability does this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) detects sensitive information (such as credit-card or health identifiers) and enforces policies to block or warn when users try to share it inappropriately.

distractors.A: Single sign-on is an identity feature, not data protection.
distractors.B: Teams channels organize conversations. None of these detect or prevent sensitive-data sharing.
distractors.C: Click-to-Run installs Office apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect and prevent oversharing of sensitive data = DLP (Microsoft Purview).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention

questions.stem: An organization wants to classify documents and emails as 'Public', 'Confidential', or 'Highly Confidential' and automatically apply encryption and visual markings based on the classification. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this?

explanation.correct: Sensitivity labels (Microsoft Purview Information Protection) classify content and can enforce protection such as encryption, access restrictions, and watermarks or headers based on the label.

distractors.A: Microsoft Bookings schedules appointments.
distractors.B: Secure Score measures security posture; it does not classify documents.
distractors.C: Conditional Access controls sign-ins, not content classification.

explanation.exam_pattern: Classify and protect content (encryption, markings) = sensitivity labels.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Sensitivity labels

questions.stem: To meet regulations, a firm must keep certain records for a fixed number of years and then dispose of them, even if users try to delete them earlier. Which Microsoft Purview capability enforces this?

explanation.correct: Retention labels and policies (Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management) keep content for a required period and can delete it afterward, helping meet regulatory recordkeeping obligations.

distractors.B: Click-to-Run installs Office apps.
distractors.C: Single sign-on is an identity feature, unrelated to retention.
distractors.D: Safe Links protects against malicious URLs, not record retention.

explanation.exam_pattern: Keep-then-dispose of content for compliance = retention labels/policies.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Retention in Microsoft Purview

questions.stem: A legal team needs to identify, place on hold, collect, and export relevant emails and documents across Microsoft 365 for a lawsuit. Which Microsoft Purview solution is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery helps legal teams identify, place holds on, collect, review, and export content across Microsoft 365 for legal and investigative cases.

distractors.A: OneDrive sync keeps files updated across devices, not legal collection.
distractors.C: MFA verifies sign-ins, unrelated to legal discovery.
distractors.D: Teams Phone is telephony, unrelated to eDiscovery.

explanation.exam_pattern: Find / hold / collect / export content for legal cases = eDiscovery (Microsoft Purview).

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): eDiscovery

questions.stem: A company adopts a security strategy summarized as 'verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach,' trusting no request by default even from inside the corporate network. Which security model is this?

explanation.correct: The Zero Trust model treats every access request as untrusted until verified, guided by three principles: verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach.

distractors.A: Perpetual licensing is a purchasing model, unrelated to a security strategy.
distractors.B: Castle-and-moat trusts anything already inside the network perimeter - the opposite of Zero Trust.
distractors.C: Open access applies no controls; it is not a security model.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Never trust, always verify' - verify explicitly / least privilege / assume breach = Zero Trust.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Zero Trust principles

questions.stem: A prospective customer's auditors want Microsoft's independent compliance reports and certifications - such as ISO 27001 and SOC audit reports - for its cloud services. Where can an organization obtain these documents?

explanation.correct: The Service Trust Portal is Microsoft's hub for audit reports, certifications (ISO, SOC, and more), and other compliance and trust documentation for its cloud services.

distractors.A: OneDrive stores personal files, not Microsoft's audit documentation.
distractors.B: The Teams admin center manages Teams, not compliance reports.
distractors.C: Microsoft Forms creates surveys and quizzes.

explanation.exam_pattern: Microsoft's audit reports and compliance certifications = Service Trust Portal.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Service Trust Portal

questions.stem: An organization wants to proactively manage privacy risks - such as identifying overexposed personal data - and automate responses to subject rights (data) requests from individuals. Which Microsoft solution is built for privacy management?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Priva (part of Microsoft Purview) helps organizations manage privacy risks for personal data and automate subject rights (data subject) requests.

distractors.A: Azure Virtual Desktop is desktop virtualization. None of these are privacy-risk solutions.
distractors.C: Teams is collaboration, not privacy management.
distractors.D: Click-to-Run installs Office apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Privacy-risk management and subject rights requests = Microsoft Priva.

references: Microsoft Learn (M365 Fundamentals): Microsoft Priva
